**`/statechart` downloads tools the first time you use it.** its command is typescript, so it needs a recent node, bun, or deno, and it names the versions when yours is too old. with `mise` installed and `TLA2TOOLS` unset, the first model check installs tlc and a temurin jdk through mise, a few hundred mb, even when `JAVA` is set. set `TLA2TOOLS`, and `JAVA` if `java` is not on your path, to skip that download. when you ask for an image of a chart, or a chart is too large to read as text, the agent installs the `pele` package from npm outside your repo. the command runs the module you pass with `--view` as code, and tlc runs java `.class` files it finds beside the spec, so run it only on a spec folder and a view you trust. the skill's `SKILL.md` and `references/render.md` describe what it installs.

edits.why: Upstream's skill downloads software on first use and says so only in its own SKILL.md and references/render.md. A reader of the README, or an agent running unattended, should meet that before the first run. The paragraph names no versions or folders, because the next sync can change them without the build noticing, and the launcher prints the runtime versions it needs. It also warns about the --view module, which statechart imports as code, and about the spec folder, which statechart passes to TLC as its library path, where TLC loads and runs any matching .class file. Upstream mentions neither. The prose is lowercase, as the rest of the README is.
